\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ be a nonnegative integer and $k$ an even nonnegative integer. The level-$k$
Fourier weight of majority on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+1$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing Fourier weight above the dimension]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_eq_zero_of_dimension_lt}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_eq_zero_of_dimension_lt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, and let $k$ be a natural number strictly greater than
$n$. Then the total Fourier weight of $f$ at level $k$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight bound at successive odd dimensions]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_next_odd_le_of_lt_top}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_next_odd_le_of_lt_top}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_next_odd_lt, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_odd_eq_zero_of_even, FABL.majority}
\difficulty{4}
Let $m$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers with $k<2m+3$. The level-$k$ Fourier weight of
majority on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+3$ is at most its level-$k$ Fourier weight
on the Boolean cube of dimension $2m+1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise stability of odd majorities]
\lean{FABL.noiseStability_majority_next_odd_lt}
\label{FABL.noiseStability_majority_next_odd_lt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.majority, FABL.noiseStability, FABL.noiseStability_majority_next_odd_comparison}
\difficulty{1}
For every integer $m\ge 0$ and every correlation parameter $0<\rho<1$, the noise
stability of majority on $2m+3$ coordinates is strictly less than that of majority on
$2m+1$ coordinates, where noise stability is computed under the correlated pair
distribution with correlation parameter $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every correlation parameter $\rho$ with $0<\rho<1$, the noise stability of majority
on $2m+1$ coordinates, viewed as a function of $m\in\mathbb{N}$, is antitone: increasing
$m$ cannot increase its value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Strict decrease of odd majority noise stability]
\lean{FABL.noiseStability_majority_odd_strictAnti}
\label{FABL.noiseStability_majority_odd_strictAnti}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.majority, FABL.noiseStability, FABL.noiseStability_majority_next_odd_lt}
\difficulty{3}
For every correlation parameter $\rho$ with $0<\rho<1$, the noise stability of majority
on $2m+1$ coordinates is strictly antitone as a function of $m\in\mathbb{N}$; that is,
its value strictly decreases whenever $m$ increases.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$ and every real number $\rho$ with $0<\rho<1$, the noise
stability at correlation $\rho$ of the majority function on $2m+1$ signs, represented as
a real-valued function, is at least $\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\rho)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Balance of odd-dimensional majority]
\lean{FABL.majority_odd_isBalanced}

\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$, the real-valued majority function on $\{-1,1\}^{2m+1}$ has
mean zero under the uniform distribution on that cube.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For every natural number $m$ and every sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^{2m+1}$, the majority
of the coordinates of $x$ equals the threshold sign of their sum divided by
$\sqrt{2m+1}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of squared normalized majority coefficients]
\lean{FABL.sum_normalizedMajorityCoefficient_sq}
\label{FABL.sum_normalizedMajorityCoefficient_sq}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, the sum over $2m+1$ coordinates of the squares of the
coefficient $1/\sqrt{2m+1}$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority noise stability bound]
\lean{FABL.exists_noiseStability_majority_odd_le_arcsine_add_inv_sqrt}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p121-b003}
\label{FABL.exists_noiseStability_majority_odd_le_arcsine_add_inv_sqrt}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.exists_noiseStability_sub_arcsine_le_of_regular_homogeneous_threshold, FABL.majority, FABL.majority_eq_thresholdSign_normalizedLinearForm, FABL.majority_odd_isBalanced, FABL.noiseStability, FABL.sum_normalizedMajorityCoefficient_sq}
\difficulty{5}
There is a constant $C>0$ such that, for every natural number $m$ and every $0<\rho<1$,
the noise stability at correlation $\rho$ of majority on $2m+1$ independent signs is at
most $\frac{2}{\pi}\arcsin(\rho)+\frac{C}{\sqrt{1-\rho^2}\sqrt{2m+1}}$.
\end{theorem}
